**Claim:** PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q` (`domain:ui` execution seat) — branch `claude/issue-6394-master-detail-derive-config-hint`. `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched` in the same label write.

## Pre-dispatch gate

**1. Thread read.** Triage comment (19:54:17Z) read in full. It carries a **ruling** and an **explicit authorization** — both relayed verbatim below.

**2. Serial — DISCHARGED.** Triage's serial note names the #6372/#6371 family. **PR #6393 merged 19:56Z**; `MasterDetailForm.tsx` on `main` now carries the `DetailEntry { id, config, status }` reshape. Nothing is in flight in `packages/plugin-form/` (the one live dev, #4929, is in `plugin-grid` / `plugin-kanban`). ⛔ Branch from current `main`, not from anything older — the file changed substantially.

**3. Premise.** Arm 2 of the resolver — `deriveDetail(...)` throwing on a schema that **loaded fine** — still returns the entry unresolved and still lands on `Loading columns…`, permanently, because the derive is not retried. ⛔ Re-derive on the merged tree; #6393 reshaped this exact function.

## Triage's ruling — option 2

> a failed derive gets the **config-hint placeholder naming `relationshipField`** as the key to set, the #5940/#6360 shape.

Rationale recorded with it, and worth carrying because it constrains the copy: it is a **configuration** error with a named remedy the code already holds — the thrown message carries the whole diagnosis (`could not find a lookup/master_detail field on "<child>" referencing "<parent>". Set relationshipField explicitly.`) and #6372 already saved it via `console.warn`. ⛔ **Do not reuse #6372's load-failure refusal placeholder** — it states the schema could not be loaded, and here it loaded fine. Triage's word: *"dishonest copy for a schema that loaded fine."*

## ⭐ Triage explicitly authorizes ONE pinned-test rewrite — and only one

My #6372 dispatch order said no assertion in `MasterDetailForm.detailChildObjectDecline.test.tsx` may be weakened. Triage has now overridden that **for exactly one assertion**, verbatim:

> This ruling **explicitly authorizes rewriting the one #6360 assertion** in `MasterDetailForm.detailChildObjectDecline.test.tsx` whose premise the body measured as inaccurate (it pins a failed derive while titled as a pending fetch) — the pending case now has an honest control in `MasterDetailForm.detailSchemaFetchFailure.test.tsx`, so no coverage is lost. **No other assertion in that file may be weakened**; #6372's dispatch-order protection stands for everything else.

The assertion in question is titled *"does NOT show the hint for a detail that names its child object, and still says `Loading columns…` while it resolves"* — its fixture (`getObjectSchema` resolving `[]` for `invoice_line`) reaches **arm 2**, not the still-pending fetch its title supposes.

⛔ **This seat's standing rule applies and is not waived by the authorization.** When a dispatch moves a pinned test, the PR body must carry **three things**:
1. the **old** assertion, verbatim;
2. the **new** one, verbatim;
3. the **ruling clause that moves it** — quote the triage authorization above.

⭐ A pin rewritten to match new behaviour without those three is the exact failure the pin exists to catch. The authorization changes *whether* you may move it, not *what you must show*.

⚠️ Triage also recorded that this rewrite **will be listed in the round report's adjudication section for the maintainer's veto window.** Make it easy to read there.

## Tests

- The failed-derive case renders the config hint naming `relationshipField`, **not** `Loading columns…`, and **not** the load-failure refusal.
- ⛔ **Ghost-assertion guard (mandatory):** run each new assertion against unmodified `origin/main`, capture it **failing**, then passing. Both readings in the PR body.
- ⛔ **Degenerate-control guard:** keep a genuinely **pending** case that still shows `Loading columns…` (the honest control now lives in `MasterDetailForm.detailSchemaFetchFailure.test.tsx`), plus a **fetch-failure** case that still shows #6372's refusal placeholder. Three arms, three distinct outcomes — assert all three, or the change is unattributable.
- The saved error must still be logged; ⛔ do not re-swallow it.

## Boundaries

⛔ Scope is `packages/plugin-form/src/MasterDetailForm.tsx` and its tests. Do not touch `LineItemsPanel.tsx`, `deriveMasterDetail.ts`'s unrelated arms, or `packages/spec`. ⛔ Do not revisit #6372's or #6360's landed arms beyond the one authorized assertion.

## Ground rules

Worktree-first: `git worktree add ../objectui-6394 -b claude/issue-6394-master-detail-derive-config-hint main && cd ../objectui-6394 && pnpm install`. ⛔ Never `git stash` — the stack lives in the common `.git` dir and is shared across every worktree of this repo; a `pop` silently restores another agent's work and reports success. ⛔ Never touch `content/docs/releases/`. Changeset: `patch`, `@object-ui/plugin-form`. Run the repo's fast checks before pushing. Open the PR as **draft** with `Fixes #6394` and report back — the PM lands it, ⛔ never self-merge.

Size: S–M. Model: opus.

← now the PENDING arm only ``` The derive arm no longer renders `Loading columns…` **at all**. So the old wait is not inconvenient, it is **impossible** — implementing triage's option 2 at all requires exactly this. There is no version of the ruled work in which that assertion survives unchanged. And the rewrite is a strengthening, not a weakening — one loose assertion became two specific ones: ``` - await waitFor(() => expect(view.container.textContent).toContain('Loading columns…')); + await waitFor(() => expect(view.queryByTestId('md-detail-no-relationship-field')).not.toBeNull()); + expect(view.container.textContent).not.toContain('Loading columns…'); ``` The control's subject — *this is not a load failure* — is unchanged and still asserted. ⛔ **Option C is rejected on principle, and it is worth naming why:** gating the new behaviour so the old pin still passes would be *making a test pass by not doing the ruled work*. It is a question of whether a forced, strengthening consequence falls inside the ruling that forced it. It does. The maintainer's veto window remains the safeguard, and both rewrites are in it. ⭐ Also correct: the rewrite's rationale was recorded **in the test file itself**, not only in the PR body.
